Tests verify observable behavior so that they survive internal refactoring; no unnecessary dependence on private methods, call sequences or implementation details.

Use reactive forms for non-trivial forms when useful.

Catch only to recover, translate, perform a defined fallback, add context or clean up; do not swallow failures.

Reviews must not require or enforce patterns the architecture has not adopted.

Check deprecation, known vulnerabilities and license of the exact selected version from official registry metadata (and upstream when necessary).

Catch only to recover, translate to an abstraction-level outcome, perform cleanup that cannot be expressed otherwise or add context preserving the original; swallowed failures and catch/log/rethrow at every layer are anti-patterns.

Update obsolete APIs from verified documentation, never invented.

When verification fails make the smallest appropriate fix and rerun until green or genuine user input is required.

When the required toolchain is unavailable report the limitation instead of editing source or changing declared SDK/Node/framework versions.
Never invent failures without a plausible execution path.
Never invent review findings to populate categories; when there are no meaningful findings say so and state the important areas that could not be verified.

Run architecture, formatting/analyzer, dependency and security checks according to the change's risk.

CI definitions stay in source control, reproduce the supported build and test commands and never hide build or test failures (no continue-on-error on build/test steps, no suppressed exit codes, no skipped failing tests).

Verify the pipeline (clean restore, builds, configured tests, no developer state, no secrets, expected artifacts) and, for containers, image build, startup, ports/configuration, non-root behavior, health probes and no stray secrets/files.
Prefer explicit registrations in small and medium projects; scan when registration volume creates genuine boilerplate, scanning the assembly that owns the services.
A singleton or hosted service needing scoped work creates a scope per operation and resolves a scoped orchestration service, not Infrastructure internals.
Inspect relevant existing code before non-trivial changes and apply the applicable rules.

Schema changes are created as new EF Core migrations from the Infrastructure project with the Api project as startup project.
Changed behavior gets maintained automated coverage at the right level.

Use tracking queries when loaded entities are modified and committed through the current Unit of Work and AsNoTracking() for read-only entity queries.
Avoid lazy loading by default; prefer an explicit query shape.
EF.CompileAsyncQuery helps only on a measured hot path where compilation/cache lookup is material.
Interceptors suit infrastructure cross-cutting behavior such as auditing, not hidden business behavior.
Never discard, overwrite, reset, clean or otherwise destroy user work to make a Git operation easier.
Never remove a worktree containing uncommitted user work.
Do not automatically stash, reset or discard local work for a merge or rebase.
Before any repository-changing operation inspect the relevant state (status, diffs) and use the minimum operation required; do not silently clean up unrelated working-tree changes.
Before a high-risk operation inspect what it would lose or rewrite.
Before committing inspect the staged diff and include only the requested logical change; do not stage unrelated modified files.
One logical change per commit with its tests; no artificial tiny commits or combined unrelated fixes.
Before pushing confirm branch and state, ensure relevant verification completed and avoid pushing unrelated local commits.
Follow the repository's commit-message convention; otherwise Conventional Commits are a useful default.
Follow an existing branch-naming convention; otherwise prefixes such as feature/, fix/, refactor/, test/, docs/, chore/ with meaningful names.
Use separate branches and worktrees for parallel implementation streams; one branch is not checked out in several normal worktrees; keep each worktree focused.
Do not commit, push, merge, rebase, reset, force-push, delete or rename branches or perform other repository-changing Git operations unless explicitly requested.
Never force-push a shared branch unless the user explicitly requests history rewriting.
A database health check is a lightweight connectivity/availability check without business queries, large scans or writes.
Keep probe responses small; detailed diagnostics only on a protected endpoint.
Avoid Error-level logs for every normal failed probe.
For repeated DELETE of an absent resource choose one convention (204 or 404) and use it consistently.
304 only for a conditional request whose cached representation is still valid, not a business 'nothing changed'.
400 for malformed JSON, invalid shape, binding failures and missing transport-level input; not for authentication failure.
406 when no acceptable representation can be produced; 415 for an unsupported request media type.
422 for structurally valid but semantically invalid requests, or 400 for both when the project deliberately uses it; follow the established convention.
428 when a contract-required precondition such as If-Match is absent.
429 with Retry-After when known for rate-limited requests; never for validation failures.
500 for unexpected internal failures via centralized handling and ProblemDetails.
502 only when acting as an intermediary that received an invalid upstream response; not every dependency failure.
503 with Retry-After when meaningful for temporary inability to serve.
504 only when acting as an intermediary whose upstream did not respond in time.
When a repeated POST must not duplicate effects consider an Idempotency-Key; reusing a key with a materially different payload returns 409.
Use standard conditional-request semantics (ETag, If-Match, 412, 428) instead of custom status codes.
Configure stable headers on the client; apply per-request values such as dynamic tokens per request or through a handler; never mutate shared DefaultRequestHeaders concurrently.
Prefer System.Net.Http.Json/System.Text.Json with explicit options when the remote contract differs; do not reuse Domain entities as remote contracts.
Hedging only for operations safe to execute several times; never hedge state-changing operations.
Do not wrap normal EF Core operations in a generic application-level retry pipeline; prefer the provider's execution strategy.

Use var when the type is obvious or unimportant; keep implementation details non-public; sealed only when deliberately not designed for inheritance.
Standard .NET naming: PascalCase for types and public members, camelCase for parameters and locals, meaningful names.
Prefer immutability when it represents the model naturally; do not force it where controlled mutation is simpler.

Distinguish confirmed findings from items needing verification and assign severity from exploitability, reachability, impact and context, never mechanically from a pattern, CVSS or OWASP category.
Do not suppress a real secret because it sits in a Development file.
Name workflows needing threat modeling instead of claiming the scan proves them secure.
Never invent exploitability.
Normalize user-controlled paths and verify they stay within the intended storage boundary (traversal, absolute-path injection, archive extraction).

Reserved choices require explicit approval before implementation.

Do not silently invent a tunable value that materially changes accepted input or observable behavior: propose it with the reason, ask for approval and record it in CUSTOM_SETTINGS.md.
Synchronize every affected surface of an approved tunable value (custom-settings).
Reserved decisions need explicit approval before implementation.
Changing an accepted project or architecture decision is Reserved.
Adopting a new architectural style or pattern (CQRS, mediator, Vertical Slice Architecture, event sourcing, microservices, Rich Domain Model or DDD tactical patterns) is Reserved.
Adding a production project, layer or assembly is Reserved.
Changing persistence boundaries (incl. multiple persistence contexts) or persistence technology is Reserved.
Adding a messaging, background processing or distributed cache infrastructure category is Reserved.
Adding a search, external storage or external identity infrastructure category is Reserved.
Adding a major library/framework is Reserved.
Replacing approved baseline technology is Reserved.
Introducing a project-wide convention or abstraction (e.g. a project-wide Result model) is Reserved.
Changing the authentication/authorization architecture is Reserved.
A breaking public API change is Reserved.
For a Reserved decision present a Decision Request (Context, Options, Recommendation, Blocked, Proceeding with) and run architecture-decision.
In an autonomous or headless run take only a policy-compliant non-Reserved path, never make a Reserved decision silently and list every unresolved Decision Request in the final report.
